summary: HTTP/2 stream flow-control blocks during very long streaming generation leading to client timeouts
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NovaDocs reported repeat client 504s and aborted streaming responses when requesting very long generations (large prefix + max_tokens) over HTTP/2. The requests enter streaming mode but stall after an extended period (typically ~60-100s) with no chunks sent; the client eventually times out. This appears after a recent routing/runtime change rolled out on 2026-03-08.

Impact:
- Multiple NovaDocs sessions failed to receive final tokens (customer-facing error).
- Affected some dedicated instances in us-west-2 and sporadically in eu-west-1.
- Customer reported production outage for a subset of users performing long-document summarization workflows.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster for NovaDocs in prod us-west-2.
- Streaming over HTTP/2 via API gateway + NGINX proxy + serving runtime.
- Typical request: system + 15 documents priming (~45k tokens) then max_tokens=120000 in generate call.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Using HTTP/2 client (httpx or curl --http2), send a streaming /v1/generate request with a very large prefix and max_tokens >= 100k.
2) Observe that initial streaming chunks may arrive, then the stream pauses for ~60-100s with no chunks.
3) Client sees stalled connection; after client timeout or proxy idle timeout, the request fails with 504 or connection reset.
Example curl reproduction:
curl --http2 -N -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
  -d '{"model":"llama-3-13b-v1","prompt":"<very long priming>","max_tokens":120000,"stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
logs:
Support logs and snippets:
- gateway request id: gw-20260310-7f5a3b (NovaDocs request)
- upstream logs: nginx: upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.2.12.45, server: api.redwood.example, request: "POST /v1/generate HTTP/2.0"
- serving-runtime: request_id=gw-20260310-7f5a3b state=STREAMING last_chunk_sent=2026-03-10T17:11:03Z stall_detected=2026-03-10T17:11:59Z kernel_thread_block=KV_SERIALIZE
- netstat trace: HTTP2 stream WINDOW_UPDATE not issued for ~75s on stream 3
- nginx proxy_read_timeout: 90s (default)
investigation_notes:
Initial hypotheses considered: KV cache eviction stalls, priority-queue starvation, load-balancer idle timeout.
Findings:
- HTTP/2 specific: trace shows stream-level flow-control window became zero and no WINDOW_UPDATE frames were sent back for ~70s while runtime was busy performing a blocking KV serialization step. This stopped the server from sending further DATA frames even though the runtime had tokens ready immediately after serialization completed.
- NGINX proxy has proxy_read_timeout=90s which plus client-side HTTP/2 flow-control pause resulted in connection termination.
- GPU utilization graphs during incidents showed low GPU activity while request was stalled, indicating the stall happened outside token generation on the critical path (I/O / serialization).
- Reproducible with a synthetic test that simulates heavy KV serialization by priming a large context and invoking max_tokens=120k; behavior only reproduced when using HTTP/2 streaming.
- Regression introduced after changeet rserve/rt-2026-03-08 that deferred some WINDOW_UPDATE handling into the same thread as KV serialization (reduced contention overall but introduced blocking race on long serializations).

Temporary mitigations tested:
- Forcing HTTP/1.1 streaming bypasses HTTP/2 flow control and avoided the stall (customer workaround).
- Reducing nginx proxy_read_timeout prevented premature disconnects but does not fix root cause.
comments: Riley Chen (Support): Customer reported first occurrence 2026-03-10 16:45 UTC. Provided request IDs and sample payloads.
Maya Patel (SRE): Reproduced locally with httpx and synthetic payload. Observed HTTP/2 WINDOW_UPDATE missing while runtime performing KV serialize. Filed internal follow-up INT-4142.

Eliot Grant (Backend Eng): Identified regression in rserve/rt-2026-03-08 that moved flow-control bookkeeping into the serialization thread. Preparing patch to send periodic WINDOW_UPDATE or offload serialization. Will test on staging.
Customer (NovaDocs): Verified workaround by switching to HTTP/1.1; request completed successfully (customer confirmed workaround acceptable short term).
resolution:
Mitigation and fix applied:
1) Hotfix deployed 2026-03-11: serving runtime v1.2.3 - offloads WINDOW_UPDATE bookkeeping to IO thread and adds a keep-alive WINDOW_UPDATE heartbeat during long blocking ops.
2) NGINX proxy config adjusted for streaming endpoints: proxy_read_timeout increased to 180s as a safety buffer while patch rolled out.
3) Added server-side guard: if stream idle > 30s due to blocking work, emit a small DATA chunk (flush) or explicit WINDOW_UPDATE to keep HTTP/2 window alive.
4) Customer advised to use HTTP/1.1 streaming as a fallback if they see stalls.
Post-deployment verification:
- NovaDocs test cases completed successfully in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 on 2026-03-11 after v1.2.3 rollout. No further incidents reported by customer.
Follow-ups:
- INT-4142 assigned to infra to instrument serialization latency and add alerts for long blocking operations (>10s).
- Engineering to consider asynchronous KV serialization and non-blocking kernels to avoid similar regressions.
resolution_summary: Served primary fix in runtime to avoid HTTP/2 flow-control starvation during long KV serialization; proxy timeout increased temporarily. Customer validated and ticket closed.
follow_up_actions: INT-4142 - instrument KV serialize times and add alerting
ENG-RT-2026 - evaluate async serialization for long-context workloads
Update streaming runbook with HTTP/2 fallback guidance
